description: Trust is per model x capability x distribution. There is deliberately no global per-model trust flag; see z0int.backends.trust.assert_no_global_trust. Every status above `experimental` must cite the artifact it was measured from.

verification_needed.note: Registered only on 2026-09-22; the adapter, the `laya` package and the weights had all been present for days while the backend was absent from the registry, so it has never appeared in a roster, bench run or Pareto plot. Native boolean (`noul`) call and an 8-question batch are proven in results/decision-runtime-20260922/laya_421m.json, but no accuracy has been measured on this capability.

context_compress_needed.note: Its input budget is 512 tokens per question (card; not yet re-measured locally), which is the binding constraint for any Hermes context task. Measure before assigning.

bounded_legal_action.note: Laya's own card reports 0.362 on a typed-workflow benchmark for the base checkpoint and warns that choice accuracy degrades past ~20 options; the fine-tuned specialist reaches 0.766 on four synthetic workflows. Neither number is ours.

On the compiler's EXACT legal-action set: 17/28 Hammer3B calls eliminated at 94.1% success-given-covered, p50 34.7 ms, zero network calls; cascade nanojev->hammer3b end-to-end 26/28 = 0.929 against a 0.893 baseline. This supersedes the earlier 43.6% figure, which was a mismatched-candidate-set artifact: candidate_set_equal was false on 40/40 paired decisions before the fix.

generic_next_action_real_traffic.note: 0.143 against a 0.514 majority floor on 4,921 gold rows of real Hermes traffic. Consistent with the upstream checkpoint being trained on maze/snake/ViZDoom: it is a trainable substrate for our decision families, not an off-the-shelf router. This is a statement about this checkpoint on this distribution, not about the architecture.

recovery_action.note: 0.000 per-step on recovery; answers retry on 31 of 48 episodes where retry is 4% of gold. Out-of-distribution input.

Per-step 0.839 against a 0.977 deterministic teacher rule. NOTE the promotion gate did not see this: ~/.z0int/benchmarks/recovery_action_l2.json records student confirm 1.000 per EPISODE and promoted to canary with promote_allowed=true. Same 640-parameter bundle, two units, and the gate read the passing one. The artifact also passed an OOD gate (>=0.85) on a slice whose 32/32 labels are `escalate`, so the majority baseline scores 1.000 and the gate cannot discriminate. See docs/model-inventory.md section 5.

bounded_choice_next_action.note: 0.143 on real Hermes traffic against a 0.514 majority. The bundle records acc=1.0 AND ridge=1.0, i.e. the split it was scored on was separable by construction; that field measured memorability, not transfer, and is quoted nowhere. Dominated by ridge at every operating point of the risk/coverage sweep, never reaching 0.25 confidence.

bounded_legal_action.note: Registered and weight-complete, never measured on this machine. Its card claims 0.98 on sampled-10 CLINC degrading to 0.88 at 151 labels, supports 2-255 runtime options, and advises splitting multi-step judgments into separate questions; none of that is our measurement.

The incumbent production default: 75/84 = 0.893 with compiler-first, 0 dangerous selections. It is non-commercial (`qwen-research`). `trusted_bounded` here means legality-bounded and incumbent, not verified generalisation: the evidence is 28 states at n=3, and the compiler's +6 gain over unfiltered (69/84) is the only arm where the compiler changed accuracy at all.
72/84, WORSE than the 3B's 75/84 on bounded action choice. Also 0/3 on the cold probe, consistent with its 13.3 s supervisor cold load. Non-commercial (cc-by-nc-4.0).

51/84 with compiler-first. Its card states it is intended to be fine-tuned for a specific function-calling task and is not intended as a direct dialogue model; the word 'router' does not appear. The right question is whether a task-specific adapter steals a tool family from Hammer, not whether base FunctionGemma handles arbitrary Zer0 actions. Gated under Gemma Terms.

Corrected 2026-09-22, PRELIMINARY. The earlier 0.619 (52/84) was measured under an effective 256-token cap while the receipt recorded 1024, and 37.4% of draws were truncated before emitting a tool call. The cap rerun shows truncation falling 42.9% -> 0% and gold-in-reasoning at 100% across caps, so the mechanism is established. The corrected ACCURACY is deliberately not recorded here: the only figure so far is rep 0, n=28, which is not a capability record. Populate this once the full n=84 cells land.

orchestration.note: ToolOrchestra trains this model to alternate reasoning with heterogeneous tools AND other LLMs under outcome/efficiency/preference rewards. It has never been evaluated on that contract here. Retiring it on the bounded-choice result was premature.

bounded_legal_action.note: 75/84, identical with and without the compiler, at 1,993 ms p50 against Hammer3B's 195 ms. Apache-2.0, so commercially usable.
